chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan about the midwife who attends to a man, is it permissible for him to marry her? He said: If she had attended to him once, twice, or three times, there is no harm. But if she had attended to him, raised him, and fostered him, then I prohibit myself from her, and my children, and in another narration, my close friend.

key_terms.تَقْبُلُ: Attends to / receives (in the context of medical/childbirth attendance)
key_terms.كَفَلَتْهُ: Fostered him / took care of him

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the midwife who delivered him or attended to him in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) nuanced ruling on marrying a midwife, distinguishing between mere attendance and deep familial integration. While limited professional interaction permits marriage, prolonged care involving upbringing (*tarbiyah*) and fostering (*kafalah*) creates a bond of modesty (*hurmah*) that the Imam personally advised avoiding, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preserving social dignity and preventing confusion in lineage or familial roles.
